task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req181-webhooks-core.md or similar) for REQ-181: a new webhook_subscriptions Ecto schema plus a Letflow.Webhooks context module (no route/controller -- that's REQ-182). Design must specify: (1) the migration -- webhook_subscriptions table, per-tenant schema with tenant_id retained (decision 0003 Decision B pattern, same as REQ-176's dlq_entries), fields: id, target_url (required), secret (hashed storage only), description (optional), event_types (array of strings), status ("ACTIVE"|"PAUSED" -- exact uppercase strings, a DIFFERENT convention from DlqEntry's lowercase status, do not unify them), consecutive_failures (integer, default 0), last_attempt_at/last_failure_at/paused_at (nullable timestamps), created_at; (2) create/2's exact behavior -- if no secret is supplied, generate one; store only a hashed form using this project's already-established hashing precedent; return the plaintext secret exactly once as hmac_secret_once in create/2's own return value, never retrievable again (list/1 and any get must never expose the plaintext or an hmac_secret_once key); (3) list/1's tenant scoping and pagination shape (mirror REQ-176's list/2 cursor convention if a plausible fit, or justify a plain list/1 if pagination isn't warranted -- state which and why); (4) update/2's reconciliation of the dual %{status: ...} / %{is_active: ...} input shapes to one single stored status value -- specify the exact mapping (is_active: true -> ACTIVE, is_active: false -> PAUSED, and how paused_at is set/cleared on each transition); (5) delete/2's tenant-scoped hard-delete and not-found-on-second-delete behavior. Design only -- no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex file content (this project's mechanical, no-exceptions rule).
acceptance_criteria: the webhook_subscriptions table lives inside each tenant's Postgres schema with a tenant_id column retained, matching decision 0003 Decision B's pattern -- verified by inspecting the migration

create/2 with no secret supplied generates one, stores only a hashed form in the database, and returns the plaintext exactly once as hmac_secret_once in its return value; a subsequent list/1 or get of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once key at all -- two explicit tests

update/2 accepts %{status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, %{is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as status "PAUSED" -- reconciling WebhookSubscription's dual status/is_active representation to one stored state
list/1 is tenant-scoped, demonstrated by a subscription created under tenant A being absent from a list/1 call scoped to tenant B
delete/2 removes the subscription such that a subsequent list/1 no longer includes it, and a second delete/2 of the same id returns a not-found error rather than a duplicate success
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
